title: Human resources and other parts of the business

match.reason: No existing point covers how HR decisions connect to operations, marketing and finance; the systems approach and internal environment points are related but broader and different ideas.

draft.title: HR and other business parts
card: Every part of a business depends on its people. HR decisions about who is hired, trained and rewarded reach all other areas.
Operations
the process of making goods or services. Skilled, well-trained staff help produce quality products with less waste.
Marketing
promoting and selling to customers. Staff who are motivated and know the product can serve customers better.
Finance
managing the business's money. Wages and training are costs, so HR decisions change what the business spends.
draft.remember: HR decisions flow into operations, marketing and finance.

a.q: A business cuts its training budget. How might this affect operations?
opts: Staff may make more errors, lowering product quality
Customers will always pay higher prices
The marketing team will automatically be larger
Wages will rise to cover the training cut
a.why: Less training can leave staff less skilled, so errors and waste may rise in producing goods or services. Prices and wages are not tied directly to a training cut.
a.clue: Operations is about making the product.

b.q: Lena's café in Hobart gives its baristas pay rises and extra training. Which effect would show up in finance?
opts: Higher wage and training costs that must be budgeted for
Lower spending on all other costs automatically
A drop in the number of staff needed
Advertising costs that are cut to nothing
b.why: Pay rises and training are money going out, so the finance area must plan for them. Better service may lift sales later, but that is not automatic, and it does not cut other costs.
b.clue: Finance deals with money coming in and going out.

a.best: Staff may make more errors, lowering product quality

b.best: Higher wage and training costs that must be budgeted for

problems.detail: The right option is the only one hedged with 'may'. Every distractor uses an absolute ('will', 'always', 'automatically'), so a student can pick the answer without knowing the idea.

The right option is clearly the longest and the only precise, plausible one. The distractors rely on extremes ('cut to nothing', 'all other costs automatically'), so the answer stands out without knowledge of finance.
The right option says costs 'must be budgeted for', but the card only says HR decisions 'change what the business spends'. The option states it more strongly than the card does.

Option (b) also says 'must', which is stronger than the card's wording.

proposal.title: HR and other business parts
card: Every part of a business depends on its people. HR decisions about who is hired, trained and rewarded reach all other areas.
Operations
the process of making goods or services. Skilled, well-trained staff help produce quality products with less waste.
Marketing

Finance

proposal.remember: HR decisions flow into operations, marketing and finance.

a.q: A business cuts its training budget. How might this affect operations?
opts: Staff may make more errors, so product quality may fall
Staff may make fewer errors, so product quality may rise
Wage costs may rise, so the business may spend more
Sales staff may know the product better, so sales may rise
a.why: Training builds the skills that help staff make quality products with less waste, so less training can mean more errors. Fewer errors would be the reverse of what the card says about training.
a.clue: What does training give staff who make the product?

b.q: Lena's café in Hobart gives its baristas pay rises and extra training. Which effect would show up in finance?
opts: Wage and training costs rise, so the café spends more
Wage and training costs fall, so the café spends less
Baristas make coffee with less waste and fewer errors
Baristas serve customers better and know the menu well
b.why: Pay rises and training are costs, so the café's spending goes up, and that is a finance effect. Better service and less waste may also happen, but they belong to marketing and operations, not finance.
b.clue: Finance is about the business's money.

a.best: Staff may make more errors, so product quality may fall

b.best: Wage and training costs rise, so the café spends more
